note: [agent-bulk] shw 4001 (269.4 MeV, 12 seg, len 80.0, the only shower in this event at or above 20 MeV) is under-clustered on its own cone. Its body is the cluster-52 group at 46.9-50.0 cm and 4.1-17.5 deg. Sitting in that same shell, unowned and tier 1, are 38017 (13.4 MeV, 2 seg) at 46.1 cm / 13.6 deg with metric 6.0, and 33012 (5.9 MeV) at 42.2 cm / 17.6 deg with metric 7.5 - both bracketed in angle AND in metric by accepted members (metrics 2.1-9.3), and both INSIDE the dashed pass-1 box on the acceptance plot while the shower's own far members sit outside it. In the picture they are the grey blobs immediately alongside the yellow body: left of it in the az +85 frame and above it in the az -55 frame. Marked 38017 and 33012 IN. Two more I did NOT mark but that point the same way: 32011 (54.4 cm / 23.2 deg, tier 1) is already owned by 38017 and would follow it, and 4002 (14.7 MeV) reads dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 against 4001 - a second shower sitting on the same start, which is a split rather than a cone-radius miss and which I am not confident enough to fold in. What I did NOT verify: the four far members 27006/29008/30009/31010 (86.7-96.8 cm at 26.8-32.1 deg, all pdg 13, all taken by pass4_angle and all outside the pass-1 box) - they are isolated stubs 40 cm past the body and I did not test whether they belong; following the pilot's evt284791 rule I did not call the shower over-clustered on them, so this verdict is a statement about what is MISSING only. Vertex: the star sits at the tip of the seed stem with the body 47 cm downstream; nothing else converges there, which is consistent with a nuecc electron but means I could not cross-check the vertex against a second prong. Not looked at: the other 12 showers, all at or below 14.7 MeV (scope rule min_kine_best 20 MeV).
